clue.text: Queen's favourite old hat for royal premiere venue

parts.note: Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was the favourite of Queen Elizabeth I
something old hat is outdated, i.e. square or unfashionable

explanation.surface: Picking a venue for a royal film premiere based on the Queen's old-fashioned favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: LEICESTER SQUARE is the London square where big film premieres, often attended by royals, take place.
explanation.definitionFit: The London square hosts cinemas famous for gala film openings attended by royalty.

clue.text: Foreign variety of thistle

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A foreign species of thistle growing in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettish is the old name for the Latvian language, a foreign tongue to English speakers.

clue.text: Republican troops question one from Baghdad?

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Republican soldiers interrogate a man from Baghdad.
explanation.definitionFit: Baghdad is the capital of Iraq, so a person or thing from there is of that country.

clue.text: City gent, one from children's home, not an especially delicate type

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
a tom is a male, as in tomcat

indicators.note: not tells us the following word is removed from the piece before it

parts.note: an orphan is a child who might be raised in a children's home
taken as written

explanation.surface: A City gentleman who grew up in a children's home is hardly a delicate sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes AN from ORPHAN, leaving ORPH. The surface's 'not an especially delicate type' reads as a denial, but 'not an' is the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Physiology classes a lean, slight body build as this type, the most fragile of the three somatotypes.

clue.text: Exhaust — one of four found on Chevrolet?

definitions.meaning: to exhaust is to wear out or weary

definitions.text: one of four found on Chevrolet?
definitions.meaning: the American spelling of a car's rubber wheel covering, fitting a US-made Chevrolet

explanation.surface: The exhaust pipe and the wheels of an American car.
explanation.definitionFit: To weary someone is to wear them out; American English spells the wheel's rubber casing this way.

clue.text: Soldiers fighting effect of drugs?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
action is combat, as in soldiers seeing action

explanation.surface: Soldiers fighting while under the effect of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug produces a response in the body, which is a typical side effect or response.

clue.text: Split half of capital

parts.note: to split is to leave, so to quit

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word of is its first letter

explanation.surface: A city divided in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the first of the two letters of 'of', giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Ecuador, high in the Andes.

clue.text: Maybe scaling down such a ropy business

definitions.text: Maybe scaling down such a ropy business

parts.words: Maybe scaling down such a ropy business
parts.note: descending a rock face on a rope is literally a 'ropy' business, though ropy usually means poor quality

explanation.surface: Downsizing a shoddy company.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers descend a cliff controlled by a doubled rope in this activity.

clue.text: Mountain, extremely testing summit unattainable

parts.note: ever means extremely, as in ever so kind

indicators.note: in a down entry the summit is the top letter, which cannot be reached and so is dropped

parts.note: testing is putting to the test

explanation.surface: A peak so hard to climb that nobody can reach the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summit unattainable' drops the top letter of TEST, leaving EST.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest peak in the world, in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Display outrageous paintings all around the restaurant

indicators.note: all around tells us the three pieces together are turned to read backwards

parts.note: to air something is to display it
OTT is over the top, i.e. outrageous
art covers paintings

explanation.surface: Shocking pictures are hung all round the dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all around' turns AIROTTART backwards as a whole, giving TRATTORIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian eating house serving simple food.

clue.text: Hot potato and fruit?

definitions.meaning: a hot potato is a controversial matter or topic of debate
fruit in the biblical sense, as in fruit of the womb, means offspring

explanation.surface: Something on the greengrocer's stall: a baked potato and some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A contentious subject is a matter under debate; children are one's progeny.

clue.text: Expressions in, Latin that one associated with old document

parts.note: id is Latin for that or it, as in id est
I is the Roman numeral one
MS is manuscript, a document

explanation.surface: Latin phrases tied to an ancient document.
explanation.definitionFit: Set phrases peculiar to a language are its characteristic turns of phrase.

clue.text: Express view on new sort of rat poison

indicators.note: the opinion-giving word follows on after the rearranged piece
a new sort of a word is the word with its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to opine is to express a view

explanation.surface: Giving opinions on a new kind of rat poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new sort of' rearranges RAT to ATR.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxic alkaloid from deadly nightshade.

clue.text: Residence accommodating British man

indicators.note: accommodating means housing something within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a home is a residence

explanation.surface: A house taking in a British lodger.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish-derived American slang for a fellow or guy.

clue.text: I'm down, so wretched, then start to grin as a result of this?

definitions.text: I'm down, so wretched, then start to grin as a result of this?

indicators.note: wretched means in a sorry state, so these letters are knocked out of order
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gloomy person suddenly cheers up and wonders why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wretched' rearranges IMDOWNSO to MOODSWIN, and 'start to' takes the G of grin. The whole clue describes the swing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden shifts from despair to cheer are abrupt changes of temper.

clue.text: Person of principle giving speech in film

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, like a mist on glass
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A principled person giving a speech in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who preaches ethics and holds strict standards of right and wrong.

clue.text: Article's advice regarding hors d'oeuvre

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tip is a piece of advice
as to means regarding

explanation.surface: A newspaper article offering advice about starters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian first course of cold meats and pickles is a starter.

clue.text: Furniture-maker failed to deal with woman's interior

indicators.note: interior means inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to sit on something is to delay acting on it
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A cabinetmaker never got round to her inner rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior' puts HER inside SAT ON, giving S-HER-ATON.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English designer of elegant furniture.

clue.text: Storm — something in a teacup, say, followed by laughter

indicators.note: say tells us the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a brew is a pot of tea
ha ha is laughter

explanation.surface: A storm in a teacup followed by mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns BREW into its sound-alike BROU. The phrase 'storm in a teacup' is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy fuss or commotion is a figurative tempest.

clue.text: Withdraw from confrontation, being behind US force

parts.note: back of is American English for behind
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: Retreating from a fight with American forces in the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat and stop pressing an argument or quarrel.

clue.text: Parts of route taken by bus or coaches

definitions.text: Parts of route taken by bus or coaches

parts.words: Parts of route taken by bus or coaches
parts.note: fare sections of a bus route, and the first half of the name of old horse-drawn coaches

explanation.surface: Sections of a journey by public transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus journey is split into fare sections, and horse-drawn coaches ran between relay posts.

clue.text: Rather complacent runner left out

indicators.note: out signals the following letter is omitted

parts.note: a runner is a smuggler, as in gun-runner

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied athlete was dropped from the team.
explanation.definitionFit: More self-satisfied, comparative of a word for complacent.

clue.text: Copper's weapon could be bloody

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a sword is a weapon

explanation.surface: A policeman's weapon may end up bloodstained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody' is a mild British swear word, so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word, and 'bloody' is a typical mild British expletive.

clue.text: Snatch some sleep, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak means as if spoken, a cue for a sound-alike

parts.note: rest is some sleep

explanation.surface: Grabbing a nap, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench or seize forcibly from someone.

clue.text: Contents of newspaper cuttings will provide summary

indicators.note: contents are what lies inside, so the letters are found within these words

explanation.surface: Newspaper clippings give an overview.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' finds APERCU inside newspAPER CUttings.
explanation.definitionFit: An apercu is a brief outline or insight.

clue.text: Sway, creeping in at regular intervals

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter

explanation.surface: A slow-moving influence that creeps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at regular intervals' takes the even letters of 'creeping in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway means rule or dominion, as does a monarch's period of power.

clue.text: One knight turns on another, displaying weapon

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for knight

indicators.note: turns tells us the word is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: another knight is a Sir

explanation.surface: A knight rounds on a fellow knight, brandishing a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Nothing pleasant is kept for later

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Nothing pleasant is held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on hold are frozen until later.

clue.text: Object about over-hasty punishment

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: an object is a thing
rash means over-hasty

explanation.surface: Objecting to a hasty penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe beating given as a penalty.

clue.text: Defend position in foreign trench so frantically?

indicators.note: frantically means wildly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A soldier holding a trench abroad with desperate energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand up for one's own interests is to argue one's case.
